title: The R4SUB Evidence Schema
text: evidence_schema_spec() returns schema table: one row per column, type, whether required, controlled vocabulary one, short description. row one observation: single check, run single asset, producing single result. Required columns must present non-missing. Nullable columns may NA.
code: spec <- evidence_schema_spec() knitr::kable(spec)

title: The R4SUB Evidence Schema
text: Four columns restricted fixed set values. Using canonical set keeps scoring aggregation consistent across sources. severity runs info (weight) critical (full weight). indicator_domain names readiness pillar check feeds: quality, trace, risk, usability. result outcome, na means check apply. source uses different labels, canon_severity() canon_result() map common aliases onto canonical set:
code: schema <- evidence_schema() schema$asset_type$allowed #> [1] "dataset"    "define"     "program"    "validation" "spec"       #> [6] "other" schema$indicator_domain$allowed #> [1] "quality"   "trace"     "risk"      "usability" schema$severity$allowed #> [1] "info"     "low"      "medium"   "high"     "critical" schema$result$allowed #> [1] "pass" "fail" "warn" "na" canon_severity(c("HIGH", "warning", "Error")) #> [1] "high"   "medium" "high" canon_result(c("PASS", "Failed", "N/A")) #> [1] "pass" "fail" "na"

title: The R4SUB Evidence Schema
text: run_id study_id tie every row back run produced . Rather set hand row, create run context let as_evidence() fill :
code: ctx <- r4sub_run_context(study_id = "STUDY01", environment = "DEV") #> ℹ Run context created: "R4S-20261025204223-wl4dieex"  ev <- as_evidence(   data.frame(     asset_type = "validation",     asset_id = "ADSL",     source_name = "pinnacle21",     indicator_id = "SD0001",     indicator_name = "Missing variable",     indicator_domain = "quality",     severity = "high",     result = "fail",     message = "Variable AGEU is missing",     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ),   ctx = ctx ) #> ✔ Evidence table created: 1 row  ev[, c("run_id", "study_id", "indicator_id", "severity", "result")] #>                        run_id study_id indicator_id severity result #> 1 R4S-20261025204223-wl4dieex  STUDY01       SD0001     high   fail

title: The R4SUB Evidence Schema
text: as_evidence() validates builds, validate_evidence() checks existing table specification: required columns present, types correct, controlled vocabularies respected. table passes validate_evidence() guaranteed score. specification function, downstream packages can rely directly rather restating column list. keeps ecosystem step: one schema, .
code: validate_evidence(ev)

title: The R4SUB Evidence Schema
text: schema change time: new column, widened vocabulary. table written one release can recognized another, every evidence table carries schema version. as_evidence() stamps , evidence_schema_version() reports . validate_evidence() reads stamp. unstamped table tolerated, table can predate versioning lose stamp round-trip CSV JSON. table stamped version release recognize, including version newer installed package, refused rather scored guesswork. table stamped older, known version, migrate_evidence() upgrades current schema: policy deliberately asymmetric: read older tables migrating forward, never pretend understand newer one. lets ecosystem move without breaking tables already written.
code: evidence_schema_version() #> [1] "1.0.0" evidence_schema_version(ev) #> [1] "1.0.0" migrated <- migrate_evidence(ev) evidence_schema_version(migrated) #> [1] "1.0.0"

title: Getting Started with r4subcore
text: r4subcore foundation R4SUB (R Regulatory Submission) ecosystem. defines three responsibilities every R4SUB pillar package depends : Run context - lightweight metadata envelope ties every piece evidence back specific study execution event. Evidence schema - fixed 17-column contract standardises findings heterogeneous sources (validators, parsers, manual checks) stored exchanged. Validation helpers - functions enforce schema every ingestion point downstream scoring profiling can always trust data.

title: Getting Started with r4subcore
text: run context captures ran assessment, study, environment, time. Every evidence row create stamped run_id study_id context, ensuring full traceability. run_id generated automatically timestamp, can supply need reproducibility tests pipelines.
code: ctx <- r4sub_run_context(study_id = "STUDY001", environment = "DEV") #> ℹ Run context created: "R4S-20261025204225-wl4dieex" print(ctx) #> <r4sub_run_context> #>   run_id:       R4S-20261025204225-wl4dieex  #>   study_id:     STUDY001  #>   environment:  DEV  #>   user:         runner  #>   created_at:   2026-10-25 20:42:25 ctx_custom <- r4sub_run_context(   study_id    = "STUDY001",   environment = "PROD",   run_id      = "RUN-2024-001" ) #> ℹ Run context created: "RUN-2024-001" ctx_custom$run_id #> [1] "RUN-2024-001"

title: Getting Started with r4subcore
text: evidence schema defines 17 columns every evidence table must contain. Call evidence_schema() inspect contract time:
code: schema <- evidence_schema() # Column names in canonical order names(schema) #>  [1] "run_id"           "study_id"         "asset_type"       "asset_id"         #>  [5] "source_name"      "source_version"   "indicator_id"     "indicator_name"   #>  [9] "indicator_domain" "severity"         "result"           "metric_value"     #> [13] "metric_unit"      "message"          "location"         "evidence_payload" #> [17] "created_at"

title: Getting Started with r4subcore
text: canon_severity() canon_result() normalise common aliases canonical values accepted schema:
code: canon_severity(c("ERROR", "warning", "Minor", "CRITICAL")) #> [1] "high"     "medium"   "low"      "critical" canon_result(c("PASS", "Failed", "Warning", "N/A")) #> [1] "pass" "fail" "warn" "na"

title: Getting Started with r4subcore
text: as_evidence() main ingestion function. supply data frame contains minimum required columns, pass run context, function: fills run_id study_id context, fills nullable columns appropriately-typed NA, sets created_at current time absent, validates result returning . can inspect resulting evidence table:
code: raw <- data.frame(   asset_type       = "validation",   asset_id         = "ADSL",   source_name      = "pinnacle21",   indicator_id     = "P21-SD0001",   indicator_name   = "Missing variable label",   indicator_domain = "quality",   severity         = "high",   result           = "fail",   message          = "Variable AGEU is missing a label",   location         = "ADSL.AGEU",   metric_value     = 0,   metric_unit      = "score",   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  ev <- as_evidence(raw, ctx = ctx) #> ✔ Evidence table created: 1 row # All 17 schema columns are present ncol(ev) #> [1] 17 ev[, c("run_id", "study_id", "indicator_id", "result", "severity")] #>                        run_id study_id indicator_id result severity #> 1 R4S-20261025204225-wl4dieex STUDY001   P21-SD0001   fail     high

title: Getting Started with r4subcore
text: validate_evidence() runs checks as_evidence() calls internally. Use receive evidence produced externally want confirm meets contract processing:
code: validate_evidence(ev)  # returns TRUE invisibly if everything is valid

title: Getting Started with r4subcore
text: combining evidence different sources indicators, use bind_evidence(). validates table individually combining, preventing schema violations silently propagating:
code: # A second finding - a passed check on the same dataset raw2 <- data.frame(   asset_type       = "dataset",   asset_id         = "ADSL",   source_name      = "r4subcore",   indicator_id     = "Q-NROW-001",   indicator_name   = "Dataset row count",   indicator_domain = "quality",   severity         = "info",   result           = "pass",   message          = "ADSL has 254 subjects",   metric_value     = 254,   metric_unit      = "count",   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) ev2 <- as_evidence(raw2, ctx = ctx) #> ✔ Evidence table created: 1 row  combined <- bind_evidence(ev, ev2) #> ✔ Bound 2 evidence tables: 2 total rows nrow(combined) #> [1] 2

title: Getting Started with r4subcore
text: evidence_summary() aggregates evidence table domain, severity, result, source, giving one-page digest findings:
code: evidence_summary(combined) #>   indicator_domain severity result source_name n #> 1          quality     high   fail  pinnacle21 1 #> 2          quality     info   pass   r4subcore 1

title: Getting Started with r4subcore
text: Evidence tables can persisted reloaded CSV, RDS, JSON format. exported file retains full schema import_evidence() can re-validate way back . RDS faithful format preserves POSIXct without string-conversion round-trip. JSON useful evidence needs consumed non-R tooling.
code: # Export to CSV tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv") export_evidence(combined, file = tmp, format = "csv")  # Import and re-validate ev_reloaded <- import_evidence(tmp, format = "csv") nrow(ev_reloaded)

title: Reading Pinnacle 21 reports into evidence
text: Pinnacle 21 report lists one row per finding: rule identifier, message, severity, dataset variable concerns, status. write small export temporary CSV vignette self-contained. real CSV Excel export shape.
code: p21 <- data.frame(   "Rule ID" = c("SD0001", "SD0002", "AD0018", "SD1077"),   Message   = c("Variable label is missing",                 "Value not in controlled terminology",                 "Expected variable is present",                 "Inconsistent value length"),   Severity  = c("Error", "Warning", "Notice", "Error"),   Dataset   = c("ADSL", "ADAE", "ADSL", "ADLB"),   Variable  = c("AGEU", "AESEV", "RACE", "LBORRES"),   Status    = c("Failed", "Warning", "Passed", "Failed"),   check.names = FALSE )  csv <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv") utils::write.csv(p21, csv, row.names = FALSE)

code: report <- read_p21_report(csv) #> ℹ Read 4 rows from /tmp/RtmpG6a06a/file1dd5540150c6.csv report #>   Rule ID                             Message Severity Dataset Variable  Status #> 1  SD0001           Variable label is missing    Error    ADSL     AGEU  Failed #> 2  SD0002 Value not in controlled terminology  Warning    ADAE    AESEV Warning #> 3  AD0018        Expected variable is present   Notice    ADSL     RACE  Passed #> 4  SD1077           Inconsistent value length    Error    ADLB  LBORRES  Failed

title: Reading Pinnacle 21 reports into evidence
text: p21_to_evidence() maps report onto evidence schema shared across ecosystem. detects rule, message, severity, dataset, variable, result columns case-insensitively, tolerates small naming differences Pinnacle 21 versions. Pinnacle 21 severities map onto evidence vocabulary: Error becomes high, Warning becomes medium, Notice becomes info. result ordinary evidence table. validates schema, scores like evidence, can combined evidence sources (Define-XML, ADRG, traceability) bind_evidence() computing Submission Confidence Index.
code: ctx <- r4sub_run_context("STUDY1", "DEV") #> ℹ Run context created: "R4S-20261025204227-wl4dieex" ev  <- p21_to_evidence(report, ctx) #> ℹ Parsed 4 rows from Pinnacle21 output #> ✔ Evidence table created: 4 rows  ev[, c("indicator_id", "severity", "result", "location")] #>   indicator_id severity result     location #> 1       SD0001     high   fail    ADSL:AGEU #> 2       SD0002   medium   warn   ADAE:AESEV #> 3       AD0018     info   pass    ADSL:RACE #> 4       SD1077     high   fail ADLB:LBORRES validate_evidence(ev)

code: # \donttest{ # Build a minimal Define-XML 2.1 document xml_txt <- '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <ODM xmlns="http://www.cdisc.org/ns/odm/v1.3"      xmlns:def="http://www.cdisc.org/ns/def/v2.1">   <Study OID="STUDY001">     <MetaDataVersion OID="MDV.001" Name="Define-XML 2.1">       <def:ItemGroupDef OID="IG.ADSL" Name="ADSL" SASDatasetName="ADSL"                         Repeating="No" Purpose="Analysis"                         def:Label="Subject-Level Analysis Dataset">         <ItemRef ItemOID="IT.ADSL.USUBJID" Mandatory="Yes"/>         <ItemRef ItemOID="IT.ADSL.AGE" Mandatory="Yes"/>       </def:ItemGroupDef>       <ItemDef OID="IT.ADSL.USUBJID" Name="USUBJID"                DataType="text" Length="20"                SASFieldName="USUBJID">         <Description><TranslatedText>Unique Subject Identifier</TranslatedText></Description>       </ItemDef>       <ItemDef OID="IT.ADSL.AGE" Name="AGE"                DataType="integer" Length="8"                SASFieldName="AGE">         <Description><TranslatedText>Age</TranslatedText></Description>         <def:Origin Type="Derived">           <def:Description><TranslatedText>Derived from RFSTDTC</TranslatedText></def:Description>         </def:Origin>       </ItemDef>     </MetaDataVersion>   </Study> </ODM>' tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".xml") writeLines(xml_txt, tmp) ctx <- r4sub_run_context("STUDY001", "DEV") #> ℹ Run context created: "R4S-20261025204218-11kz8bwc" ev <- define_xml_to_evidence(tmp, ctx) #> ℹ Define-XML: found 1 dataset(s) (ItemGroupDef) #> ℹ Define-XML: found 2 variable definition(s) (ItemDef) #> ℹ define_xml_to_evidence: 4 rows generated #> ✔ Evidence table created: 4 rows nrow(ev) #> [1] 4 # }

title: r4subcore 0.3.0
text: Add evidence_diff(), compares two evidence tables reports changed : findings added, removed, changed, whether change made submission better worse. Rows matched indicator asset, duplicate keys collapse worst row, result ordered regressions first team sees act . turns evidence table something can track run run, raw material behind higher-level trend views sci_diff().

title: r4subcore 0.2.1
text: hash_id() now hashes memory rlang::hash() instead writing temporary file calling tools::md5sum every call. result shape (32-character hex string, deterministic) roughly three orders magnitude faster, removes main bottleneck building trace model generating identifiers large submission. exact hash values change; opaque identifiers, persisted contract. Add check_define_consistency() define_variables(). first compares variables declared Define-XML variables actually present datasets emits evidence : match, variable documented absent data, variable present documented. Drift Define-XML data common submission problem, makes scored quality indicator. second extracts dataset variable pairs Define-XML file.

title: r4subcore 0.2.0
text: Add read_p21_report(), loads Pinnacle 21 validation report disk (CSV natively, Excel optional readxl package) ready p21_to_evidence(). team can now go report Pinnacle 21 already produces scored evidence without hand-building table. canon_severity() now recognizes “notice”, severity Pinnacle 21 uses lowest level, mapping onto info. evidence table now carries schema version. as_evidence() stamps , evidence_schema_version() reports current version version given table, migrate_evidence() upgrades table written older release. validate_evidence() tolerates unstamped table refuses unknown newer version, table written future release silently mis-scored. Fix import_evidence(): CSV JSON round-trip leave -NA character column (example source_version) typed logical, failed validation. Every schema column now coerced back declared type import. Add evidence_schema_spec(), publishes evidence schema tidy table (column, type, required, allowed values, description) use data dictionary reference. Add vignette: “R4SUB Evidence Schema”, formal specification evidence table shared across ecosystem. Add adrg_to_evidence() adrg_sections() Analysis Data Reviewer’s Guide coverage. Given structured summary standard ADRG sections guide contains, emits usability evidence: missing required sections fail, missing recommended sections warn. machinery covers SDRG via source_name. Add evidence_sources(), reference table supported planned evidence sources format, pillar, entry point. Harden define_xml_to_evidence() real-world Define-XML variability. now matches elements local name, reads files regardless mix ODM def: namespaces (plain //ItemGroupDef query silently missed namespace-prefixed elements). Derivations resolved referenced MethodDef Origin carries inline text, missing optional elements tolerated, partially parseable file now returns informative warning. Clarified package DESCRIPTION: “R4SUB” expands “Ready Submission” (previously “R Regulatory Submission”, inconsistent rest ecosystem).
